decision: Use a deterministic end-to-end calibration integration gate that composes the real DAG planner, synthetic workload command handler, resource probe, calibration harness, and collector with mocked qrexec transport.

correctness.reason: Component-only tests cannot detect contract drift across plan binding, workload lifecycle, sampling order, cleanup, and collector provenance. Using the real modules while replacing only qrexec/process boundaries exercises the actual contracts without requiring Qubes in CI.

robustness_security.winner: fail-closed lifecycle plus cleanup fault injection
robustness_security.reason: Partial distributed starts and probe failures must trigger cleanup attempts for every worker. Collector provenance mismatch remains a hard failure. The integration gate does not weaken qrexec policy or introduce privileged monitoring.

latency_resources_regression.reason: It adds no qrexec traffic, VM startup, daemon, or database. ResourceProbe uses mocked /proc input and zero-duration sleeps; synthetic workload execution is state-backed with a fake executor PID. Regression surface is test-only.

alternatives_rejected.reason: Low cost but misses cross-module lifecycle and provenance drift.

alternatives_rejected.approach: real Qubes integration as the only gate
alternatives_rejected.reason: Highest fidelity but unavailable in hosted CI and too expensive/noisy for every change. It remains a later qualification gate.
Adds runtime state, attack surface, resources, and failure modes without being necessary to validate the existing composition.

qa.happy_path: DAG plan -> SyntheticWorkload start -> ResourceProbe samples -> stop -> collector, with five deterministic samples per worker.
faults: partial start failure rolls back all workers before sampling
probe failure stops all successfully started workers
stop failure remains fail-closed and attempts cleanup on every worker
collector rejects wrong Git SHA provenance
concurrent sampling preserves deterministic worker event ordering

failure_lessons: A failed stop transport cannot prove immediate remote cleanup. The workload remains duration-bounded by the worker-side service, but qualification must not claim clean shutdown without positive stop evidence.
Integration tests should replace only environmental boundaries; mocking the planner, workload service, probe, and collector together would recreate the same blind spot as component-only testing.
Parallel sampling can remain deterministic because Promise.all preserves input ordering; event emission should keep topology order rather than completion order.
next_gate: Add explicit cleanup confirmation/reconciliation for ambiguous stop failures, then run this same lifecycle through dig.SyntheticWorkload and dig.ResourceProbe inside real worker Qubes.
